newsitem.title: UK: S&P - tough time for German insurers, France brighter.
newsitem.headline: S&P - tough time for German insurers, France brighter.

text.p: German insurers may suffer difficult conditions and a significant consolidation, while the recently hard-hit French insurance industry now has brighter prospects, Standard & Poor's said on Wednesday.

"German insurers, and in particular the middle market sector, may be set to suffer a difficult environment and substantial consolidation, echoing the high-profile difficulties France has undergone in recent years," S&P said in a report.
"The German economy seems to have overcome the integration of its eastern states and is an attractive potential market for insurance companies.
"The French insurance industry has had a rougher ride...but prospects are brighter, particularly for the major players," the report said.

On the life side, S&P said positive factors for France and Germany were low levels of guaranteed payouts to policyholders -- in contrast with the U.S. market -- and an aging population coupled with a lack of funded pension provisions. This created a new market for existing life insurers, it said.
"In France, Standard & Poor's sees a substantial new market for long-term savings and risk transfer life products.

"In Germany, opportunities for foreign entrants might be created in the life sector should new entrants offer higher returns than the somewhat staid levels currently offered to policy holders," the agency said.
S&P said it expects both French and German markets to polarise, with niche players at one end and the major groups at the other. "This may lead to mergers for medium-sized groups."
Some German insurers have started to differentiate levels of risk, and technical margins are still doing well, although not so well as previously, S&P said.

"The country has had no particular downturns in real estate or volatility in bond or equity values. However, shareholders could in the future become more demanding of German insurance companies," it said.
